device.nameMissingOnDevice: No name on the device yet

reset.title: Factory reset: {{device}}
reset.warning: **Caution:** The device will be reset to factory settings. Wi-Fi access, password, name, schedules and all other settings will be lost.
reset.apMode: Afterwards the device starts in **AP mode** (its own Wi-Fi “shelly…”) and disappears from this network. It is no longer reachable from here.
reset.snapshotHint: A snapshot of the current config is saved automatically beforehand. The inventory entry is kept with the status “Reset”.
reset.snapshotFailed: The snapshot before the reset failed ({{reason}}). The reset was **not** performed.
reset.override: Reset anyway without a snapshot. The current config will not be documented.

sites.intro: Each site (house, customer, holiday flat …) has its own inventory, its own templates and its own log. At the top right you choose which site you are working in. A scan stores the devices found in the selected site; a device that already belongs to another site is only reported and can be moved in the detail view.

templates.intro: A template bundles settings that are applied to several devices of the current site, translated for Gen1 and Gen2+. Before applying, you see per device what will change.

templateEditor.intro: Only ticked settings belong to the template; entering a value ticks the setting automatically. Everything else stays unchanged on the devices.
templateEditor.networkWarning: Caution: wrong network values make devices unreachable; then only a factory reset on the device helps. Test on one device first. SSID and Wi-Fi password are never changed.
templateEditor.networkHint: With “Static” the app assigns addresses in ascending order from “IP from” (by floor, location and name) and skips used ones. Devices that already have a static IP in the range keep it. When applying, the IP can be changed per device.
templateEditor.sta1Hint: Only devices with a second Wi-Fi set up.

templateApply.title: Apply template: {{name}}
templateApply.previewHint: Preview based on the newest snapshot per device; when applying, each device is read afresh.
templateApply.noConfigSnapshot: No snapshot with config yet. The changes are determined when applying.
templateApply.networkWarning: This template changes network settings. Beforehand the app checks that each planned IP is in the network, is free and belongs to no other device, and afterwards looks for the device at the new address. The check does not detect devices without a web server (phones, printers …): best choose the range outside the DHCP pool. Test on one device first.
templateApply.apWarning: Without an AP password the access point is not switched on for devices where it is off: the firmware requires a password for this. The other settings are applied anyway.
templateApply.snapshotHint: Before any change a snapshot is saved automatically per device. If it fails, the device stays unchanged. Passwords are not stored.
templateApply.unreachableAt: not reachable at {{ip}} – please scan again

mqtt.title: MQTT
mqtt.hint: The MQTT password is not stored but entered when applying. Gen2+ needs a reboot after MQTT changes.

device.title: Device name
device.hint: Writes the name to the device; the name in the app takes it over. Placeholders {name} (current name), {floor} (floor), {location} (location), {kind} (type), {id}, {mac}; empty placeholders are dropped. Gen1 allows at most 30 characters.

time.title: Time and coordinates
time.hint: Coordinates are used for sunrise and sunset. Gen1: a fixed time zone switches off automatic detection.

eco.title: Eco mode and LED
eco.hint: For Gen1 eco mode is not officially documented and is therefore not set. The LED option exists only on some Gen1 models.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.hint: “Bluetooth on/off” and “Observer” exist only on older firmware; newer firmware controls this automatically.

wifiAp.title: Device Wi-Fi access point
wifiAp.hint: Not for Gen1: there AP and Wi-Fi client exclude each other. To switch it on, the firmware (2.0 and later) requires an AP password; it is entered when applying.

script.title: Script
script.hint: Created or updated by name. If the code on the device is the same, the script is left untouched.

unsupported.password: AP password needed, not switched on
unsupported.inactive: not set up on the device
unsupported.no_ip: no free IP in the range
unsupported.gateway_cloud: without a gateway, Gen1 needs the cloud switched off first
unsupported.name_empty: Name would be empty (floor, location and type missing)
unsupported.name_too_long: Name too long for this device
